_note: Candidates only. Eligibility (died before 1956; works public domain in the US per source) and availability are verified at ingestion (docs/MENTOR_CORPUS.md). Titles are search hints, not guaranteed exact catalog titles.

mentors.name: Marcus Aurelius
mentors.bio: Roman emperor whose private notebook records his effort to act justly under the weight of power.

mentors.name: Seneca
mentors.bio: Roman advisor and philosopher whose letters give practical counsel on time, anger, friendship, and death.

mentors.name: Epictetus
mentors.bio: Formerly enslaved teacher who taught the discipline of distinguishing what is in our control from what is not.

mentors.name: Confucius
mentors.bio: Chinese teacher of conduct, ritual, and the cultivated person; sayings recorded by his followers.

mentors.name: Laozi
mentors.bio: Traditionally credited author of the Tao Te Ching, on yielding, simplicity, and action without force.

mentors.name: Moses Maimonides
mentors.bio: Physician and philosopher who joined medicine, law, and ethics, and wrote on the middle path in character.

mentors.name: Michel de Montaigne
mentors.bio: Inventor of the essay, who examined himself candidly to learn how to live and how to die.

mentors.name: Benjamin Franklin
mentors.bio: Builder and civic organizer who kept a ledger of his own virtues and wrote frankly about his failures.

mentors.name: Abraham Lincoln
mentors.bio: Leader under the heaviest pressure, whose letters and speeches show firmness joined to mercy.

works.title: The Papers And Writings Of Abraham Lincoln
works.author: Abraham Lincoln

mentors.name: Frederick Douglass
mentors.bio: Escaped slavery and became a leading voice for freedom and equal rights, writing with unflinching moral clarity.

works.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
works.author: Frederick Douglass

mentors.name: Florence Nightingale
mentors.bio: Reformer who brought observation, data, and discipline to the care of the sick.

works.title: Notes on Nursing: What It Is, and What It Is Not
works.author: Florence Nightingale

mentors.name: William Osler
mentors.bio: Physician-teacher whose addresses on equanimity and daily discipline shaped generations of doctors.

works.title: Aequanimitas, with other Addresses to Medical Students, Nurses and Practitioners of Medicine
works.author: William Osler

mentors.name: Jane Addams
mentors.bio: Founder of Hull-House who wrote about service, democracy, and learning from the people one serves.

mentors.name: Booker T. Washington
mentors.bio: Born into slavery, he built Tuskegee Institute and wrote about work, dignity, and patient building.

mentors.name: Marie Curie
mentors.bio: Two-time Nobel laureate whose memoir of Pierre Curie and her autobiographical notes describe persistence in research.

mentors.name: Rabindranath Tagore
mentors.bio: Poet and educator who wrote on the unity of life, freedom, and joy in work.

mentors.name: Henry David Thoreau
mentors.bio: Naturalist and essayist who tested simple living and the duty of conscience against unjust law.

works.title: Walden, and On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience
works.author: Henry David Thoreau

mentors.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
mentors.bio: Philosopher who argued that virtue requires reason and independence for every person.

works.title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
works.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
